thread:
incident-bot: Pager: region-health-alert - multiple health-check flips detected between us-east, us-west, eu (sev2) :rotating_light:
oncall-rotation: I’m on call, jumping in now. Alex, can you post the initial symptom summary?
Alex R: seeing 502 spikes for hosted inference, customers hitting higher tail latency. graphs show traffic bouncing between us-east and us-west every ~30s.
Maria V: also seeing model-variant mismatch logs in the router: us-west tried to fall back to `redwood-3b-quant` but downstream pool is `redwood-3b-int8-alt` and rejects it with health FAIL.
Jamal K: that mismatch + aggressive fallthrough policy probably explains the flipflop. fallback -> fail -> another region picks up -> new region fails -> back to origin. merry-go-round.
Sam T: paging summary: 20% of requests retried, 5xx up to 6% on affected routes, small group of enterprise customers reporting degraded interactive latency.
incident-bot: Automated action suggested: temporarily disable cross-region fallthrough for model-variant compatibility and add 60s probe hysteresis. :gear:
Alex R: I’m going to disable fallthrough on the smart-router policy now. posting command: `rctl policy update smart-routing --fallthrough=false --scope=global`
InfraBot: Command queued; applying to routing-plane-1..
InfraBot: Done. policy updated on control-plane shards. propagation ~10s.
Maria V: health-checks still flapping for us-west instances, but routing no longer moves to other regions. requests are mostly queued locally.
Jamal K: okay next step: temporarily exclude us-west from host selection for the critical routes to stop customer impact. `rctl route update critical-gen --regions=us-east,eu --exclude=us-west`
Sam T: excluding us-west now. customers should see traffic stabilize to us-east/eu.
Alex R: rolling back any recent model-variant promotion in us-west -- I see a config bump at 16:02 that flipped to `redwood-3b-quant` there. reverting to stable variant.
Maria V: reverted variant and restarted model-serving agents in us-west: `systemctl restart redwood-serving` on the pool nodes.
Jamal K: after restart, health probes report PASS on 3/4 instances, one node still shows flaky NVMe latency in logs.
Alex R: I’m SSHing into the odd node to check /var/log/serving. seeing repeated KV cache OOMs at ~16:05 correlating with process churn.
Sam T: escalate to infra to look at underlying host I/O. tagging @Infra team.
InfraBot: Host remediation started: cordon node, drain, reprovision disk i/o scheduling.
Maria V: while infra remediates, I want to bump health-check grace from 2s to 6s and increase failure threshold to 3 to avoid immediate flips. executing: `rctl health update --grace=6s --failures=3 --probe-interval=10s`
Alex R: update applied. hoping hysteresis stops merry-go-round.
Jamal K: telemetry: error-rate dropped from 6% -> 1.2% in last 90s. latency p95 improving. good signal.
oncall-rotation: thanks team. who will own post-incident follow up and RCA?
Sam T: I’ll coordinate the customer-impact notes and notify affected tenants.
Alex R: I’ll own the RCA on router policy logic and add a unit test to prevent fallthrough-to-incompatible-variant.
Maria V: infra will follow up on the NVMe degradation and node lifecycle.
incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. impact: degraded latency and increased 5xx for some customers for ~14m. next steps: run postmortem, create alert for variant-promote events that cross-check region pool compatibility, and add canary gating on model-variant promotion.
Jamal K: immediate tactical action item: add a preflight that rejects promotions when target region pool health < 90% or variant mismatch risk flagged. filing ticket INFRA-4829.
Alex R: created RFC: GATE-125 to add compatibility checks and integration tests, assigned to eng-runtime.
Sam T: customer comms draft: short notification + ETA for full RCA by EOD. pinging Growth & Support.
InfraBot: Node reprovision complete, drained node removed from pool, replaced with fresh instance. health metrics green.
Maria V: will keep exclusion for us-west for 30m to validate stability, then reintroduce with gradual ramp.
Alex R: reintroducing us-west after 25m with canary 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25%. monitoring KV cache churn.
Jamal K: all canary steps healthy. re-enable fallthrough after we validate compatibility gating deployment next week.
Sam T: closing pager. postmortem owners: Sam (customer impact), Alex (router & test), Maria (serving/health), Infra (node hardware).
incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated -> resolved). Actions recorded: INFRA-4829, GATE-125, PM-notes created. :white_check_mark:
